Advanced Features

Advanced analysis tools, optimization, and low-level interfaces.

Residual Workspace

Low-level residual evaluation infrastructure for model implementations.

Automatic Differentiation

Cached workspace and sparsity detection for efficient Jacobian computation.

Parameter System

Differentiable parameter system for optimization and sensitivity analysis.

Powerful.ParameterSlice — Type
ParameterSlice

Maps a contiguous slice of the parameter vector p to a model field.

Fields

  • model_name::Symbol: Model type (e.g., :PV, :Branch)
  • field_name::Symbol: Field name (e.g., :pg, :x)
  • model_indices::AbstractVector{Int}: Which model instances (Vector or CuVector)
  • param_range::UnitRange{Int}: Contiguous range in p vector (always contiguous!)
  • field_ref::AbstractVector: Direct reference to model.field array

Design

The paramrange is always contiguous (e.g., 1:3, 4:9), allowing us to use view(p, paramrange) as a contiguous destination. Combined with model_indices, this unifies with the residual system's single-indexed gather/scatter pattern.

source
Powerful.ParameterizedSystem — Type
ParameterizedSystem

System with optimizable parameter mapping.

Workflow

# Setup (once, outside optimization loop)
psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, 1:10)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :qg, 1:10)
finalize_parameters!(psys)  # Rebuilds models once

# Hot loop (type-stable, zero allocations)
function objective(p)
    scatter_parameters!(psys, p)  # Works with Float64 or Dual!
    y = solve_power_flow(psys.sys)
    return loss(y)
end
source
Powerful.add_parameter! — Method
add_parameter!(psys, model_name, field_name, instances)

Mark a subset of model instances' fields as optimizable parameters.

NOTE: This only tracks what needs to be made generic. Call finalize_parameters!(psys) to actually rebuild the models with generic field types.

Arguments

  • psys::ParameterizedSystem: Parameter system
  • model_name::Symbol: Model type (e.g., :PV, :Branch)
  • field_name::Symbol: Field name (e.g., :pg, :x)
  • instances: Model instance indices (UnitRange or Vector{Int})

Example

psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)

# Mark parameters (no rebuilding yet)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, 1:10)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :qg, 1:10)  # Same model, different field
add_parameter!(psys, :Branch, :x, 1:50)

# Rebuild models once for all marked fields
finalize_parameters!(psys)
source
Powerful.compute_parameter_jacobian! — Method
compute_parameter_jacobian!(B::SparseMatrixCSC, psys::ParameterizedSystem,
                             cache::ADCache,
                             y::AbstractVector, p::AbstractVector)

Compute parameter Jacobian dg/dp efficiently using cached sparsity and coloring.

Uses colored forward-mode automatic differentiation to compute only the nonzero entries of the Jacobian. Much faster than naive approach for sparse systems.

Performance

For ACTIVSg 70k (135,800 residuals, 1,000 parameters):

  • Naive: 1,000 evaluations × 140ms = 140 seconds
  • Colored: ~50 evaluations × 140ms = 7 seconds
  • 20x speedup from matrix coloring!

Arguments

  • B::SparseMatrixCSC: Pre-allocated sparse matrix (same sparsity as psys.sparsity_dgdp)
  • psys::ParameterizedSystem: System with cached sparsity pattern
  • adcache::ADCache: Autodiff cache for residual evaluation
  • y::AbstractVector: Current state vector
  • p::AbstractVector: Current parameter vector

Example

# Setup (compute sparsity once)
sys = SystemModel(am, models)

psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, 1:100)
finalize_parameters!(psys)

# IMPORTANT: Create cache AFTER finalization!
adcache = ADCache(psys.sys)

parameter_sparsity_pattern!(psys, adcache)  # Cache sparsity

# Allocate sparse Jacobian matrix
B = Float64.(psys.sparsity_dgdp)

# Compute dg/dp at current operating point
p = gather_parameters(psys)
dae = DAE(cache.address_manager)  # Get current state
y = dae.y

compute_parameter_jacobian!(B, psys, cache, y, p)

# Now B contains ∂g_i/∂p_j for all nonzero entries

Returns

  • nothing: B is modified in-place
source
Powerful.finalize_parameters! — Method
finalize_parameters!(psys::ParameterizedSystem)

Rebuild models with generic field types for all marked parameters.

This should be called ONCE after all add_parameter! calls and BEFORE optimization. It rebuilds each affected model once with the necessary fields made generic.

Example

psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, 1:10)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :qg, 1:10)
finalize_parameters!(psys)  # Rebuilds PV model once with pg, qg generic

# Now scatter works with Dual numbers
p_dual = ForwardDiff.Dual.(p, ones(length(p)))
scatter_parameters!(psys, p_dual)  # Works!
source
Powerful.gather_parameters — Method
gather_parameters(psys::ParameterizedSystem) -> Vector

Extract current parameter values from model fields into flat vector.

Returns parameter vector p with length psys.total_params.

Uses unified gather! kernel from gather_scatter.jl (same as residual system).

source
Powerful.parameter_pullback! — Method
parameter_pullback!(p_bar::AbstractVector, psys::ParameterizedSystem,
                    cache::ADCache,
                    y::AbstractVector, p::AbstractVector,
                    y_bar::AbstractVector)

Low-level reverse-mode AD primitive: Compute parameter gradient from upstream gradient.

This is a Vector-Jacobian Product (VJP): Given upstream gradient dy/dp, compute downstream gradient dp/dp using implicit differentiation.

Mathematics

For power flow: g(y(p), p) = 0

By implicit function theorem:

dy/dp = -(dg/dy)^-1 · dg/dp = -J^-1 · B

Given upstream gradient y_bar = dloss/dy, compute:

p_bar = dloss/dp
      = (dy/dp)^T · y_bar
      = -B^T · (J^-T · y_bar)
      = -B^T · lambda

where lambda solves: J^T · lambda = y_bar (adjoint system)

Arguments

  • p_bar::AbstractVector: Output parameter gradient dloss/dp (modified in-place)
  • psys::ParameterizedSystem: Parameter system (must be finalized)
  • adcache::ADCache: Autodiff cache (created after finalization)
  • y::AbstractVector: State vector at solution (from power flow solve)
  • p::AbstractVector: Current parameter vector
  • y_bar::AbstractVector: Upstream gradient dloss/dy

Performance

  • Time: O(solve) + O(adjointsolve) + O(coloredjacobian)
  • Independent of number of parameters!
  • Much faster than forward-mode for many parameters

Example

# Setup
psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, 1:100)
finalize_parameters!(psys)
adcache = ADCache(psys.sys)

# Forward pass: solve power flow
p = gather_parameters(psys)
y = solve_power_flow_somehow(psys, p)

# Compute loss and upstream gradient (your custom logic)
v = get_bus_voltages(sys, y)
loss = sum((v .- 1.0).^2)
y_bar = compute_dloss_dy(y)  # Your gradient computation

# Reverse pass: compute parameter gradient
p_bar = similar(p)
parameter_pullback!(p_bar, psys, cache, y, p, y_bar)

# Now p_bar contains dloss/dp

Use Cases

  1. Custom optimization: Manually implement gradient descent
  2. Composed systems: Integrate with neural networks, other simulators
  3. Sensitivity analysis: Compute dy/dp without full objective
  4. Building blocks for rrule: Use in ChainRules definitions

Returns

  • nothing: p_bar is modified in-place
source
Powerful.parameter_sparsity_pattern! — Method
parameter_sparsity_pattern!(psys::ParameterizedSystem, cache::ADCache)

Automatically detect and cache the sparsity pattern of dg/dp using AD probing.

This function probes each parameter to detect which residuals depend on it. The sparsity pattern is cached in psys.sparsity_dgdp for reuse.

Algorithm

For each parameter p[i]:

  1. Set p[i] = Dual(p[i], 1.0) (all other parameters remain Float64)
  2. Scatter parameters to model fields
  3. Evaluate residuals g(y, p) using the provided cache
  4. Extract dual parts to find nonzero ∂gj/∂pi
  5. Record sparsity pattern

Arguments

  • psys::ParameterizedSystem: Parameter system (must be finalized)
  • adcache::ADCache: Autodiff cache for residual evaluation (must be created AFTER finalize_parameters! so it sees generic fields)

Performance

  • Time: O(nparams × residualeval_time)
  • One-time cost (result is cached)
  • For 1000 params on ACTIVSg 70k: ~5-10 seconds

Example

sys = SystemModel(am, models)

psys = ParameterizedSystem(sys)
add_parameter!(psys, :PV, :pg, 1:100)
finalize_parameters!(psys)

# IMPORTANT: Create cache AFTER finalization!
adcache = ADCache(psys.sys)

# Detect sparsity (computed once, then cached)
sparsity = parameter_sparsity_pattern!(psys, adcache)

# Now cached
@assert !isnothing(psys.sparsity_dgdp)
@assert !isnothing(psys.colors_dgdp)

Returns

  • SparseMatrixCSC{Bool, Int}: Sparsity pattern (also cached in psys)
source
Powerful.scatter_parameters! — Method
scatter_parameters!(psys::ParameterizedSystem, p::AbstractVector)

Copy parameter values from flat vector p into model fields.

Works with both Float64 and Dual numbers after finalize_parameters! is called.

Uses unified scatterunmasked! kernel from gatherscatter.jl (same as residual system).

Performance

  • Time: O(n_params) - simple indexed assignment
  • Allocations: Zero (after first compile for each type)
  • Typical: 1-10 μs for 1000 parameters on CPU
source

Variable and Residual Accessors

Generic accessors for DAE variables and residuals.

Powerful.get_all_res — Method
get_all_res(sys::SystemModel, g::AbstractVector, model::Symbol, res::Symbol) -> Vector

Get all residual values across all instances (in internal order).

Returns a view into the residual vector.

Example

# Get all bus power balance residuals
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
workspace = setup_powerflow_newton(prob)
bus_residuals = get_all_res(sys, workspace.cache.iter_dae.g, :Bus, :p)
source
Powerful.get_all_vars — Method
get_all_vars(prob::ACPowerFlowProblem, y::AbstractVector, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) -> Vector

Get all values for a variable across all instances (in internal order).

Returns a view into the state vector, not a copy.

Examples

# Get all bus voltages from solution
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())
voltages = get_all_vars(prob, sol.dae.y, :Bus, :v)

# Get all PQ load powers
pq_powers = get_all_vars(prob, sol.dae.y, :PQ, :p)
source
Powerful.get_res — Method
get_res(sys::SystemModel, g::AbstractVector, model::Symbol, res::Symbol, ext_key) -> T

Get residual value using external key.

Examples

Powerful.get_var — Method
get_var(prob::ACPowerFlowProblem, y::AbstractVector, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, ext_key) -> T

Get variable value using external key (e.g., bus number).

Generic function that works for any variable in any model by combining:

  1. IndexOrder: external key → internal array index
  2. AddressManager: model/variable → DAE addresses
  3. State vector: addresses → actual values

Arguments

  • prob::ACPowerFlowProblem: Power flow problem (contains sys and address_manager)
  • y::AbstractVector: State vector (from solution, workspace, or custom)
  • model::Symbol: Model name (:Bus, :PQ, :PV, etc.)
  • var::Symbol: Variable name (:v, :theta, :p, etc.)
  • ext_key: External key for lookup (bus number, or tuple for composite keys)

Returns

  • Variable value (type matches y element type)

Examples

# After solving - query solution
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())
v = get_var(prob, sol.dae.y, :Bus, :v, 4001)

# During iteration - query workspace state
workspace = setup_powerflow_newton(prob)
v_iter = get_var(prob, workspace.cache.iter_dae.y, :Bus, :v, 4001)

# Query trial point during line search
v_trial = get_var(prob, workspace.y_trial, :Bus, :v, 4001)

# PQ load power (composite key: bus number + load id)
p = get_var(prob, sol.dae.y, :PQ, :p, (4001, "1"))

# Branch flow (composite key: from bus, to bus, circuit id)
p_flow = get_var(prob, sol.dae.y, :Branch, :p_i, (4001, 4002, "1"))

Errors

  • If prob.sys.order is nothing: Error (IndexOrder required)
  • If external key not found: KeyError from IndexOrder
  • If model/variable not found: Error from AddressManager
source
Powerful.get_var_by_index — Method
get_var_by_index(prob::ACPowerFlowProblem, y::AbstractVector, model::Symbol, var::Symbol, idx::Int) -> T

Get variable value using internal array index (1-based indexing).

Faster than get_var() since it skips external→internal mapping. Use when you already have internal indices.

Arguments

  • prob::ACPowerFlowProblem: Power flow problem
  • y::AbstractVector: State vector
  • model::Symbol: Model name
  • var::Symbol: Variable name
  • idx::Int: Internal array index (1-based)

Example

# Direct access by internal index (no external key lookup)
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())
v = get_var_by_index(prob, sol.dae.y, :Bus, :v, 1)  # First bus in internal ordering
source
Powerful.get_vars_dict — Method
get_vars_dict(prob::ACPowerFlowProblem, y::AbstractVector, model::Symbol, var::Symbol) -> Dict

Get all values as a dictionary keyed by external keys.

Useful for exporting results with semantic bus numbers.

Example

# Get bus voltages indexed by external bus number
prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys, PowerInjection())
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())
voltages = get_vars_dict(prob, sol.dae.y, :Bus, :v)
# Dict(1 => 1.06, 2 => 1.045, 4001 => 1.02, ...)

I/O and Reporting

Report generation and output formatting.

Powerful.ColumnPreferences — Type
ColumnPreferences

Configuration for column selection and naming.

Fields

  • use_descriptions::Bool: Use ModelParam.description vs. field name
  • include_units::Bool: Append "(MW)", "(pu)" to column names
  • column_style::Symbol: Naming style - :compact (pfrom), :short (pfrom (MW)), :verbose (full description)
  • include_id::Bool: Include instance ID column
  • include_vars::Union{Nothing, Vector{Symbol}}: If set, only include these variables
  • exclude_vars::Vector{Symbol}: Exclude these variables
  • include_params::Bool: Include model parameters
  • exclude_params::Vector{Symbol}: Exclude these parameters
source
Powerful.FormattingPreferences — Type
FormattingPreferences

Configuration for value formatting in reports.

Fields

  • float_precision::Int: Default decimal places (default: 4)
source
Powerful.ReportConfig — Type
ReportConfig

Complete configuration for power flow report generation.

Fields

  • units::UnitPreferences: Unit conversion preferences
  • formatting::FormattingPreferences: Value formatting preferences
  • columns::ColumnPreferences: Column selection and naming

Examples

# Default configuration
config = ReportConfig()

# Customize units only
config = ReportConfig(units=UnitPreferences(voltage=:kv, angle=:rad))

# Customize multiple aspects
config = ReportConfig(
    units = UnitPreferences(voltage=:kv, power=:pu),
    formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision=6),
    columns = ColumnPreferences(exclude_vars=[:internal_state])
)

# Use preset configurations
config = AllPerUnit
config = AllPhysical
source
Powerful.UnitPreferences — Type
UnitPreferences

Configuration for unit conversions in reports.

Fields

  • power::Symbol: Power units - :physical (MW/MVAR) or :pu
  • voltage::Symbol: Voltage units - :pu (default) or :kv
  • angle::Symbol: Angle units - :deg (default) or :rad
  • impedance::Symbol: Impedance units - :pu or :ohm
  • base_mva::Float64: System base power in MVA (default: 100.0)

Examples

# Default: physical power, pu voltage, degrees
UnitPreferences()

# All physical units
UnitPreferences(voltage=:kv, power=:physical)

# All per-unit
UnitPreferences(power=:pu, voltage=:pu, angle=:rad)
source
Powerful.collect_model_table — Method
collect_model_table(sol::MultiIslandSolution, model_name::Symbol; config=Default)

Collect model data from a multi-island solution, merging results from all islands.

Returns a unified table containing data from all islands. Instances are included from all islands based on their external keys.

Note: MultiIslandSolution is defined in src/solvers/power_flow_api.jl. This function handles the I/O-specific concern of merging data tables across islands.

Arguments

  • sol::MultiIslandSolution: Multi-island power flow solution
  • model_name::Symbol: Name of model type (e.g., :Bus, :Branch)
  • config::ReportConfig: Configuration for units, formatting, and columns

Example

sol = solve(ACPowerFlowProblem(sys), RobustNewton())  # May return MultiIslandSolution
bus_data = collect_model_table(sol, :Bus)
df = DataFrame(bus_data)
source
Powerful.get_available_outputs — Method
get_available_outputs(model_type::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Vector{Symbol}

Get all available output variables for a model (DAE variables + observations). These are the variables that can be included in reports via collect_model_table.

Example

julia> get_available_outputs(Branch)
6-element Vector{Symbol}:
 :p_from
 :q_from
 :p_to
 :q_to
 :p_loss
 :q_loss

# Use in report generation
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(include_vars=[:p_from, :p_loss]))
report = collect_model_table(sys, :Branch; config=config)
source
Powerful.get_default_outputs — Method
get_default_outputs(model_type::Type{<:AbstractModel}) -> Vector{Symbol}

Get the default output variables for a model (those shown in reports by default). This is a subset of get_available_outputs - observations with default_output=false are excluded unless explicitly requested via include_vars.

Example

julia> get_default_outputs(Branch)
4-element Vector{Symbol}:
 :p_from
 :q_from
 :p_to
 :q_to

# Losses are available but not shown by default
julia> get_available_outputs(Branch)
6-element Vector{Symbol}:
 :p_from
 :q_from
 :p_to
 :q_to
 :p_loss  # Available but not default
 :q_loss  # Available but not default
source
Powerful.print_model_table — Method
print_model_table(sol, model_name::Symbol; config=Default, kwargs...)

Pretty-print model data as formatted table using Pretty Tables.jl.

This function activates the config.formatting preferences (floatprecision, etc.) which are otherwise unused by `collectmodel_table()`.

Arguments

  • sol: PowerFlowSolution or MultiIslandSolution
  • model_name::Symbol: Model to print (e.g., :Bus, :Branch)
  • config::ReportConfig: Report configuration
  • kwargs...: Passed to PrettyTables.jl

Examples

# Terminal output (default)
print_model_table(sol, :Bus)

# Customized precision using config
config = ReportConfig(formatting = FormattingPreferences(float_precision = 2))
print_model_table(sol, :Bus; config=config)

# Compact format
print_model_table(sol, :Branch; config=Compact)
source
Powerful.PowerFlowReport — Type
PowerFlowReport

Structured power flow report data, format-agnostic.

Contains all information needed to generate a report in any format (text, markdown, JSON, etc.). The report captures system metadata, convergence information, and model result tables.

Fields

  • n_buses::Int: Number of buses in the system
  • n_branches::Int: Number of branches
  • n_pv::Int: Number of PV generators
  • n_pq::Int: Number of PQ loads
  • converged::Bool: Whether the power flow converged
  • iterations::Int: Number of solver iterations
  • final_residual::Float64: Final residual norm (infinity norm)
  • sections::OrderedDict{Symbol, NamedTuple}: Model data tables in presentation order

Example

# Build report from solution
report = build_powerflow_report(sol, config)

# Render as text
text = format_text(report)
println(text)

# Future: other formats
# markdown = format_markdown(report)
# json = format_json(report)
source
Powerful.build_powerflow_report — Method
build_powerflow_report(sol::PowerFlowSolution, config::ReportConfig) -> PowerFlowReport

Build a structured power flow report from a solution.

Extracts system metadata, convergence statistics, and model result tables according to the provided configuration. The resulting report is format-agnostic and can be rendered in multiple ways.

Arguments

  • sol::PowerFlowSolution: Power flow solution from solve()
  • config::ReportConfig: Report configuration (units, formatting, columns)

Returns

PowerFlowReport containing all report data

Example

prob = ACPowerFlowProblem(sys)
sol = solve(prob, RobustNewton())

# Build report with custom config
config = ReportConfig(units=UnitPreferences(voltage=:kv))
report = build_powerflow_report(sol, config)

# Render as text
text = format_text(report)
source
Powerful.format_text — Method
format_text(report::PowerFlowReport; config=Default, backend=:text) -> String

Render a PowerFlowReport in various formats using PrettyTables.jl.

Generates a complete power flow analysis report with:

  • System summary (bus/branch/generator/load counts)
  • Convergence information (status, iterations, residual)
  • Model result tables (buses, generators, loads, branches)

Arguments

  • report::PowerFlowReport: Report data structure
  • config::ReportConfig: Report configuration (for formatting precision)
  • backend::Symbol: Output format (:text, :markdown, :html, :latex)

Returns

Formatted string suitable for console or file output

Example

config = ReportConfig(formatting=FormattingPreferences(float_precision=2))
report = build_powerflow_report(sol, config)

# Text output (default)
text = format_text(report; config=config)
println(text)

# Markdown output (for documentation)
md = format_text(report; config=config, backend=:markdown)
write("report.md", md)

# HTML output (for web reports)
html = format_text(report; config=config, backend=:html)
write("report.html", html)
source
